transcript.text:
Ah, Mr. Potter, please, come in. Have a seat. Thank you for coming back so promptly.

We've just finished reviewing the results from your initial diagnostic charms, and... well, it's not quite what we expected, to be honest. We're seeing some rather unusual magical residue in your neural pathways – it seems to be a lingering effect, most likely from your extensive exposure to dark magic during the war. It's not matching any standard post-combat magical diagnosis we have on record.

I'm going to need to run much deeper, more specialised scans over the next several days to truly understand what we're dealing with here. And frankly, Mr. Potter, I can't yet tell you whether this is something you'll recover from. We simply don't have enough information right now.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I see. I expected as much, I suppose. It's been getting worse, the headaches and the... disorientation. It's like there's a fog in my head sometimes, and I can't quite shake it off. I'm not... I'm not sure I'm ready to hear that this might not be something I can just... get over. But I'll do whatever you need me to do, Doc. I've faced worse, I suppose.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I understand, Mr. Potter. The headaches and disorientation you've described, that 'fog' – it all correlates with what we're observing. And I hear you. I know this isn't easy news to receive, especially when you've already been through so much. It's a daunting prospect, certainly, to consider something that might not simply 'get over'.

But your willingness to cooperate is precisely what we need right now. We *will* get to the bottom of this, one step at a time. The next few days will involve some more in-depth diagnostic spells, nothing painful, but they will be thorough. They'll help us map out exactly what this residue is doing, and how it's interacting with your magical core and, yes, your neural pathways. That information is crucial before we can even begin to discuss treatment options, or indeed, prognosis.

Just take it one day at a time, Mr. Potter. We're here to guide you through it.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Right. One day at a time. I can do that. I mean, I have to, don't I? I've got... people counting on me. Ginny, and... the others. I can't just... fall apart, not now. So, what's the first step? When do we start? I'm ready, as ready as I'll ever be, I suppose.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
That's precisely the spirit we need, Mr. Potter. And it's admirable, that concern for others. But for now, your primary focus needs to be on yourself and these diagnostics. You can't help others effectively if you're not well yourself.

The first step is simply to get you comfortable. We'll be bringing you back to a private room here at St. Mungo's – just for a few days – to ensure we can run these scans without interruption and monitor any changes. We'll start with a detailed cognitive mapping spell, which will give us a clearer picture of those neural pathways we discussed. It's a bit lengthy, but entirely non-invasive, more like a prolonged thought-link than anything painful.

We can start as soon as you're ready to be settled in. Nurse Pomfrey's assistant, Healer Trainee Patel, will show you to your room and explain the schedule for today. Rest assured, you'll be well looked after.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Nurse Pomfrey... it's good to hear that name. She's... she's been through this sort of thing before, hasn't she? At least I know I'm in capable hands. I'll... I'll be ready whenever you are. Lead the way, Patel. I'll follow. I'm not... I'm not sure how to feel about all of this, but I know I need to do it. So, let's get it over with, shall we?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Indeed, Mr. Potter, Nurse Pomfrey has seen more than her fair share of unusual cases and is one of the most experienced Healers on staff. Her oversight, even in an administrative capacity these days, ensures that our protocols are always of the highest standard. You are absolutely in capable hands here.

It's perfectly natural to feel a mix of emotions right now. This is uncharted territory for us all, but facing it head-on is the best approach. 'Getting it over with' is a good way to look at it – the sooner we have a complete picture, the sooner we can begin to formulate a plan.

Healer Trainee Patel is just outside the door. She'll take excellent care of you and guide you through the initial steps. I'll be checking in personally once the first set of scans is complete.

transcript.text: All right. I'll... I'll try to be as cooperative as I can. Patel, you said? She'll be there to... to explain what's happening? It's just... it's all a bit overwhelming, to be honest. Thanks for... for being so... straightforward about it all. I appreciate that, even if it's not exactly the news I wanted to hear.

You're doing remarkably well, considering. Your willingness to face this, even with the uncertainty, is exactly what we need. And you're welcome. My job is to give you the clearest picture possible, difficult though it may be. We'll navigate this together. Now, go with Patel. I'll see you shortly.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Right. I'll... I'll do my best to stay calm and not... not be a nuisance. transcript.speaker: antagonist
